headline: BRTC launches women-only 'Pink Buses' in 3 cities
summary: The new service is now operational in Dhaka, Chattogram, and Bogura to ensure safer and more comfortable commuting for women.
details: The Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation (BRTC) has introduced a special 'women-only' bus service, known as Pink Buses, in Dhaka, Chattogram, and Bogura.
The service was inaugurated by the Minister for Road Transport and Bridges, Rabiul Alam, to provide women with a safer and more comfortable travel experience.
The initiative aims to reduce harassment and overcrowding in public transport, allowing women to commute with greater ease and security.
While the service has started in three major cities, there are plans to expand the women-only bus service to every district in the country.
However, the first day of operations faced a setback as a Balaka bus collided with one of the new Pink Buses on its first day of service.
caption:
Safe commutes for women! BRTC has launched 'Pink Buses' in Dhaka, Chattogram, and Bogura.

The Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation (BRTC) has introduced a special 'women-only' bus service, known as Pink Buses, in Dhaka, Chattogram, and Bogura.

The service was inaugurated by the Minister for Road Transport and Bridges, Rabiul Alam, to provide women with a safer and more comfortable travel experience.

The initiative aims to reduce harassment and overcrowding in public transport, allowing women to commute with greater ease and security.

While the service has started in three major cities, there are plans to expand the women-only bus service to every district in the country.

However, the first day of operations faced a setback as a Balaka bus collided with one of the new Pink Buses on its first day of service.

headline: 1,472 AI cameras launched to curb highway extortion on Dhaka-Chattogram route
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed says the new automated system will record extortion and automatically issue fines for traffic violations.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has inaugurated an 'Auto Super Fine System' featuring AI cameras at Meghna Ghat in Sonargaon, Narayanganj, to restore order on the highways.
A total of 1,472 AI cameras have been activated on the Dhaka-Chattogram highway to specifically target and reduce the prevalence of extortion in the transport sector.
The minister stated that any extortion activities, whether carried out by vehicle owners or laborers, will now be recorded by these cameras, leaving a digital trail of the crime.
Beyond extortion, the AI system will automatically detect traffic violations such as overspeeding, illegal parking, and driving on the wrong side of the road.
Once a violation is detected, a notice of the case and the fine will be sent directly to the registered owner's mobile phone, allowing them to pay the penalty from home.
The Home Minister also issued a strict warning that three-wheelers will no longer be allowed on the highways, restricting their movement to markets, filling stations, and feeder roads.
caption:
1,472 AI cameras are now watching the Dhaka-Chattogram highway to stop extortion and traffic crimes.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has inaugurated an 'Auto Super Fine System' featuring AI cameras at Meghna Ghat in Sonargaon, Narayanganj, to restore order on the highways.

A total of 1,472 AI cameras have been activated on the Dhaka-Chattogram highway to specifically target and reduce the prevalence of extortion in the transport sector.

The minister stated that any extortion activities, whether carried out by vehicle owners or laborers, will now be recorded by these cameras, leaving a digital trail of the crime.

Beyond extortion, the AI system will automatically detect traffic violations such as overspeeding, illegal parking, and driving on the wrong side of the road.

Once a violation is detected, a notice of the case and the fine will be sent directly to the registered owner's mobile phone, allowing them to pay the penalty from home.

The Home Minister also issued a strict warning that three-wheelers will no longer be allowed on the highways, restricting their movement to markets, filling stations, and feeder roads.
